headline: Australia's duty of care bill would let users switch off algorithmic feeds
dek: On November 24, Labor struck a deal with the Greens to pass Australia's digital duty of care legislation through the Senate, ABC News reported. The bill would let Australians 16 and over turn off algorithm-driven feeds and see only accounts they follow, and it raises the maximum penalty to 5% of a platform's global revenue. It had not passed as of that report, no start date was given, and small businesses with low-risk websites would be exempt.
why: If many Australians switch to following-only feeds, posts from accounts they do not follow will reach fewer of them. Followers and email lists would carry more of the load for businesses that market there.
doThis: If you sell to customers in Australia, start tracking follower growth and email signups next to organic reach so you have a baseline before the rules take effect.
